intro: Plain-language questions a consultant can ask in the first conversation. Meridian's answers are pre-filled; change any of them to see the placement move.

questions.prompt: How does service leadership describe service in budget meetings?

options.label: A cost of keeping customers happy that we try to hold down
A margin line with its own revenue and margin targets
A growth engine sold as uptime or output subscriptions

questions.prompt: Is service priced separately from the equipment?

options.label: No. It is bundled into the sale or covered by warranty
Yes. Time and materials, plus service contracts
We charge for uptime, usage, or output rather than labor

questions.prompt: Are technicians dispatched against a customer-owned installed asset?

options.label: Rarely. Most visits are to a location, not a specific machine
Sometimes. It depends on the job type
Almost always, to a specific serialized unit
The asset is ours; the customer pays for what it does

questions.prompt: Do contracts carry entitlements such as response time or covered parts?

options.label: No. Most work is billed as it happens
Some basic coverage, with few written terms
Yes. Response-time commitments, covered parts, and PM schedules
Contracts guarantee uptime or output, with penalties

questions.prompt: What share of jobs are scheduled appointments versus break-fix on equipment?

options.label: Mostly booked appointments such as installs, visits, and inspections
Roughly even
Mostly break-fix and planned maintenance on equipment
Most issues get solved remotely before anyone travels

questions.prompt: When a job does not close on the first visit, what is usually missing?

options.label: The customer was not available or the time slot slipped
The right part, or the machine's service history
Specialist know-how; the technician needed an expert
Telemetry or performance data to prove the outcome

questions.prompt: How does the customer judge a good service visit?

options.label: Arrived in the window and was courteous
Machine back up, fixed the first time
Got the right answer fast, often without a visit
The contracted uptime or output was met this month
Nobody. Service is measured on cost and customer satisfaction
A service leader with their own P&L
Shared with sales, measured as recurring subscription revenue

presets.label: A booked-visit operator run to cost
